stories.title: Orchestrating autonomous agents to decompile a first-person shooter
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how to structure infrastructure and harnesses when running autonomous AI agents across large-scale software reconstruction tasks.

stories.title: Multi-agent collective intelligence enables recursive self-improvement in AI
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how distilling collective intelligence from multi-agent systems enables recursive self-improvement beyond human supervision. You will learn how models can serve as their own optimizers and evaluators on complex frontier tasks.

stories.title: Solving SQLite's single-writer limitation without modifying source code
stories.why_read: Read this to discover how SQLite can handle concurrent writes across multiple processes without modifying its core code. You will learn the history of SQLite write bottlenecks and the technical trade-offs of previous workarounds.

stories.title: Plimsoll reports verifiable isolation tiers for untrusted code
stories.why_read: Learn how Plimsoll executes untrusted agent code while programmatically reporting and enforcing verifiable isolation boundaries. It introduces an explicit mechanism for setting floor requirements across process, container, kernel, and VM tiers.

stories.title: Dynamic shredding of semi-structured JSON yields massive speedups
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how dynamic shredding dramatically accelerates analytical queries on semi-structured OpenTelemetry data. You will gain a clear mental model of how decomposing arbitrary JSON attributes into columnar structures eliminates query bottlenecks.

stories.title: Jointly training tool creation and use improves agent reasoning
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how jointly training tool generation and invocation inside a single policy enables language models to craft functional APIs tailored to their own capabilities. You will learn how multi-axis reward feedback addresses the decoupling failure modes common in existing tool-augmented systems.

stories.title: Containers fail as security boundaries making microVMs necessary
stories.why_read: Read this to understand why Linux containers fail as security boundaries and how microVMs provide true workload isolation. You will learn the architectural trade-offs, VMM ecosystems, and emerging sandbox tools for secure compute.

stories.title: Versioned filesystems provide transactional state for disposable execution sandboxes
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how to design transactional file storage for ephemeral execution environments. You will learn how treating sandbox runs as database commits enables zero-copy branching and secure state persistence.

stories.title: LLMD unifies open model serving across multiple hardware accelerators
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how LLMD provides a unified, cross-platform inference server for open-weight models across major hardware targets. You will learn about its built-in runtime primitives, including continuous batching, paged attention, and speculative decoding.

stories.title: Query pushdown in Postgres foreign data wrappers requires negotiation
stories.why_read: Read this to understand the mechanistic trade-offs of query pushdown when bridging Postgres and ClickHouse. You will learn how foreign data wrappers balance remote query execution against raw row transfer.

stories.title: Common replication assumptions underestimate data loss in large clusters
stories.why_read: Read this to understand why naive independence assumptions fail when calculating disk failure risks in distributed systems. You will gain a realistic mental model of how replication factors impact actual data durability.

stories.title: Why BoxLite is replacing libkrun with a custom VMM
stories.why_read: Read this to understand the architectural limitations of libkrun that prompted BoxLite to build its own micro-VM monitor from scratch.

stories.title: Choreography-derived runtime enforcement executes finite multiparty protocols in Rust
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how Hibana enforces multiparty communication protocols at runtime without exploding endpoint types. You will learn how global choreographies can be projected into compact, allocation-free state machines in Rust.

stories.title: Projecting global protocol choreography into rust endpoint roles
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how hibana-quic implements executable choreography in no_std Rust to strictly enforce protocol order and state transitions across network endpoints.

stories.title: Building an agent harness from scratch to pass intelligence tests
stories.why_read: Read this to understand the core architecture of an AI agent harness beyond just the underlying model. You will learn how to construct an agent execution loop from scratch to manage context and run tools.

stories.title: Megakernels underperform optimized separate kernels during Mac inference
stories.why_read: Read this to understand why combining operations into a single megakernel fails to outperform separate kernels when memory bandwidth limits projection throughput on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Sandboxed JavaScript programs minimize context overhead from tool calls
stories.why_read: Read this to learn how executing tool calls inside a sandboxed JavaScript runtime reduces token usage. You will discover how filtering intermediate data keeps your context window clean.

stories.title: Tool-using agent benchmarks fail their advertised executable contracts
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how hidden defects in simulated tool environments distort agent benchmark evaluations. You will learn how to audit tool implementations against executable contracts to identify false scoring assumptions.
